text:
Evan: quick FYI 1 onboarding sample app hit a nasty auth double-refresh loop on Android 14 emulators after ProGuard shrink. Repro and logs below; Authenticator seems to run twice and we issue duplicate token refreshes.

Sara: oh no. can you paste the logs and the OkHttp client config?

Evan: logs:
```
W/OkHttp: response for https://api.redwood.ai/token: code=401 message=Unauthorized
I/Authenticator: starting token refresh (requestId=abc123)
I/Authenticator: refresh complete, new token saved
I/Authenticator: starting token refresh (requestId=abc123)
I/Authenticator: refresh complete, but original call already retried -> 401 again
```
Client snippet:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor()) // attaches access token
  .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator())
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .build()
```

Mike: this smells like the interceptor attaching an old token while the authenticator is concurrently refreshing, which triggers another request and fires the authenticator again. On Android the scheduler + proguard/shrinker timing makes the race more common.

Ashley: two practical fixes: 1) make AuthInterceptor consult a shared atomic flag/Mutex that indicates an in-flight refresh and avoid re-attaching/stashing a retry while refresh in progress; 2) set `.retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` for auth-sensitive clients so OkHttp's low-level retries don't overlap your auth logic. Also scope TokenAuthenticator to only act on responses that include `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` (or other explicit challenge), not every 401.

Mike: avoid `synchronized` on Application scope; moving refresh to a single-threaded CoroutineScope + `refreshMutex.withLock { ... }` removed a lot of flaky behavior for us.

Evan: implemented mutex + disabled retryOnConnectionFailure for the auth client. Much improved. Still see rare flakiness on emulator but overall green. Post-change CI snippet:
```
[RUN] onboarding-sample - serial
I/Authenticator: starting token refresh (requestId=def456)
I/Authenticator: refresh complete
I/OkHttp: retried request with new token -> 200
[PASS] onboarding-sample
```

Sara: great. we should update the sample app README and add a short note in the SDK docs about interceptor vs authenticator ordering and recommended Android patterns (Mutex/Coroutine, avoid double-refresh). This is a legit gotcha for customers.

Ashley: also discovered a missing ProGuard keep rule: obfuscation changed Token.equals/hashCode which broke AtomicReference comparisons in Auth code. Add to sampleapp proguard-rules.pro:
```
-keep class com.redwood.sdk.auth.Token { *; }
```

Evan: opened draft PR `devex/disable-retry-auth-mutex` with tests and README updates. CI: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/2123 (android-ci)

android-ci: Build 2123 succeeded (emulator API 34, 3/3 instrumentation tests passed) :white_check_mark:

Mike: follow-ups: 1) add an e2e test that simulates concurrent 401s to catch regressions; 2) add ProGuard note to SDK migration guide; 3) consider exporting a `safeAuthClient()` helper in the SDK that sets `.retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` and recommended timeouts so customers get a safe default.

Evan: agreed. I'll open tickets for 1+2 and draft a small RFC for the helper. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
